overview.workspaceText: The tenant boundary for documents, people, billing, integrations, and support data.
overview.knowledgeBaseText: The indexed collection used to retrieve evidence for an answer.

overview.conversationText: A sequence of messages from the employee playground, widget, or Custom API.

overview.customerPath: Install the hosted widget when you want CacaNode to provide the browser UI and conversation flow.

gettingStarted.signInText: Open the dashboard with an active workspace account. Tenant administrators and regular users can upload employee-only sources; only administrators can make sources customer-visible.
gettingStarted.uploadText: Start with a text-based policy, product guide, FAQ, or spreadsheet smaller than 20 MB.
gettingStarted.indexText: Do not test the source until its status is Completed.
gettingStarted.askText: Use the playground and open the answer citations to verify the source.
gettingStarted.uploadBody: Open Documents, choose Upload document, select the visibility, and submit the file. Clear, well-structured source material produces the easiest citations to review.
gettingStarted.uploadWarning: Scanned PDFs and legacy Office files are not supported. Export image-only scans with OCR and save old .doc or .xls files in a current format before upload.
gettingStarted.indexBody: New uploads move through Pending and Processing. A Completed file is available for retrieval. A Failed file includes an error message; correct the source and upload it again.
gettingStarted.testBody: Open the Chat playground, ask a question answered by the document, and review the source cards beneath the response. Open a citation to see the relevant page, sheet, cell range, section, or text unit in the document viewer.
gettingStarted.testTip: Test both a question the source can answer and one it cannot. This checks that your answer instructions and evidence boundary behave as expected.
gettingStarted.widgetDescription: Use the hosted widget for customer-facing answers.
gettingStarted.apiDescription: Use the Pro API for a server-owned chat experience.
gettingStarted.workspaceDescription: Set customer answer instructions and review quotas.

playground.askBody: The playground is an authenticated employee channel. It can retrieve both EMPLOYEE_ONLY and CUSTOMER_AND_EMPLOYEE documents. Start a new conversation for a new subject so prior messages do not influence the context.
playground.askTip: Ask the same question your customer or teammate would use. Natural phrasing is a better retrieval test than copying a document heading verbatim.
playground.sourcesBody: Assistant responses can include source citations with snippets and structured locations. Select a citation to open the document viewer focused on the relevant page, section, spreadsheet cells, or indexed unit.
playground.sourcesNote: No citation usually means the model did not return grounded evidence for that response. Rephrase the question, check indexing, and verify the source contains the answer.
playground.historyBody: The history panel works like a ChatGPT-style conversation list. Search by conversation title or message content, then reopen a result without losing its prior turns and citations.
playground.historyRecent: Recent conversations are ordered by activity.
playground.historyTitle: The first user message supplies a short default title.
playground.historyPrivate: History belongs to the signed-in playground user, not to website visitors.
playground.manageBody: Create a conversation when switching topics. Hide threads that are no longer useful to remove them from your history; they may still be retained for workspace analytics. Customer conversations from the Widget and Custom API are managed separately under Conversations.

documents.pdfDescription: Text-based PDF documents; scanned image-only PDFs are excluded.
documents.wordDescription: Current Word format; legacy .doc files are excluded.
documents.spreadsheetDescription: Current Excel workbooks and CSV data; legacy .xls files are excluded.
documents.limitText: Files larger than 20 MB are rejected. Split large sources into coherent documents instead of arbitrary fragments so citations stay understandable.
documents.pendingText: the upload was accepted and is waiting for ingestion.
documents.processingText: text and structure are being extracted and indexed.
documents.completedText: the source can be retrieved and cited.
documents.failedText: ingestion stopped; review the error and upload a corrected file.
documents.employeeVisibility: Available to authenticated workspace users in the employee playground. It is never exposed in Widget or Custom API evidence.
documents.customerVisibility: Available in employee and customer channels. Only a tenant administrator can assign customer-visible access.
documents.visibilitySecurity: Visibility is an evidence boundary, not just a display filter. Customer answers and signed evidence URLs exclude employee-only sources.
documents.viewerBody: Select a completed document to open its viewer. Citation links can focus a precise indexed unit or chunk. Depending on the source, metadata can include page number, section path, heading, sheet name, cell range, table identifier, or text offsets.
documents.viewerVerification: Use citation snippets and source locations to verify the answer against the original material. A citation score is retrieval relevance, not a guarantee that the source statement is correct.
documents.manageBody: The document list supports text search plus status, file type, and access filters. Deletion removes the document from the workspace and retrieval pipeline. Existing chat text may remain in conversation history, but deleted evidence can no longer be opened or retrieved.
documents.deleteWarning: Deletion is intended to be permanent. Confirm that no employee or customer workflow still depends on the source before removing it.

widget.adminNote: Widget configuration, managed tokens, branding, icons, and origins are administrator-only settings.
widget.configureBody: Open Settings → Widget to set the display name, welcome message, six-digit hex primary color, bottom-left or bottom-right position, and active state.
widget.chooseIcon: Choose the built-in icon or upload a custom icon.
widget.branding: Custom branding can hide CacaNode attribution. Starter workspaces continue to show it.
widget.originsBody: Add exact HTTP or HTTPS origins such as https://www.example.com. Do not include a path. When the list is non-empty, requests must come from one of the configured parent origins.
widget.originsSecurity: List every production and staging origin that hosts the widget. An empty list does not provide an origin allowlist; use explicit origins for production deployments.
widget.generateText: CacaNode creates a token scoped to widget:chat. Its secret is displayed once.
widget.saveText: Store the value as CACANODE_WIDGET_TOKEN in your deployment environment or secret manager.
widget.rotationWarning: Rotating the managed token invalidates the previous widget credential. Update the deployed embed value at the same time.
widget.embedIntro: Use the exact script URL shown in Widget settings and inject the environment value during deployment.
widget.embedPlacement: Place the script near the end of the body element or in the site-wide layout. The async attribute keeps widget loading off the critical rendering path.
widget.browserToken: A browser widget token is visible to visitors in page source and network requests. Its limited widget:chat scope and origin checks are the security boundary.
widget.neverApiToken: Never reuse an api:chat token in browser code.
widget.keepInactive: Keep the widget inactive until configuration and source visibility have been tested.
widget.revoke: Revoke or rotate tokens after suspected exposure.
widget.evidenceText: Customer citations can contain a signed public_url. Links expire (the current default is one hour) and only open a document while it remains completed, customer-visible, and associated with a valid integration. They do not expose employee-only or incomplete sources.
widget.visibilityDescription: Control which sources customer channels can retrieve.
widget.supportDescription: Review conversations and tickets created by visitors.

workspace.adminNote: The settings described on this page are restricted to tenant administrators.
workspace.instructionsBody: Answer instructions guide responses in the Website Widget and Custom Chat API. Use them to define tone, audience, escalation rules, and constraints that should apply across customer conversations.
workspace.instructionsBlank: Instructions must not be blank and are limited to 4,000 characters.
workspace.instructionsChanges: Changes apply to subsequent customer answers.
workspace.instructionsRestore: The restore action replaces the custom text with the platform default.
workspace.instructionsBoundary: Instructions do not grant access to employee-only documents or override citation visibility.
workspace.instructionsTip: Write operational instructions, not source facts. Keep changing policies in documents so answers can cite them and content owners can update them independently.
workspace.messagesDescription: Shared by chat surfaces and reset on the billing anniversary or plan quota window.
workspace.membersDescription: Active members subject to the plan limit.
workspace.storageDescription: Stored document size measured in MB.
workspace.quotaBody: When a live total is over limit, existing data is preserved but new growth is blocked until usage is reduced or the plan is renewed or upgraded. Message quota exhaustion blocks new chat messages.
workspace.billingTrial: New registrations begin with a time-limited Pro trial; trial expiration falls directly to Starter.
workspace.billingIntervals: Paid Pro can be monthly or annual. Annual plans retain monthly message windows anchored to the paid activation date.
workspace.billingRenewal: Renewals are manual hosted checkouts. Early renewal extends from paidThroughAt and does not reset the current quota window early.
workspace.billingGrace: Paid expiration enters a three-day grace period. Grace keeps the final Pro quota window and does not grant another allowance.
workspace.billingFallback: After grace, the workspace falls back to Starter. Existing documents, users, webhook configuration, and branding preferences remain stored.
workspace.billingDowngrade: A Starter change during paid Pro is scheduled after prepaid access and grace; during trial it ends the trial immediately.
workspace.billingSecurity: A checkout return URL is not proof of payment. CacaNode activates entitlements only after verified payment processing and exposes the current state in Billing settings.
workspace.webhooksDetail: endpoint creation, testing, delivery, and rotation
workspace.analyticsDetail: detailed scoped trends and popular questions
workspace.brandingDetail: hide CacaNode branding in the widget
workspace.starterFeatures: The hosted widget and dashboard summary remain available on Starter within the active plan limits. Always use the live plan catalog and Billing feature badges as the source of current commercial limits.
workspace.tokensBody: Create separate tokens for separate environments and purposes. Available scopes are widget:chat and api:chat; the secret is shown only at creation or rotation.
workspace.tokensName: Name tokens by surface and environment.
workspace.tokensExpiry: Use optional expiration dates for temporary integrations.
workspace.tokensRotate: Rotate a normal token to replace its secret, or revoke it to stop access.
workspace.tokensManaged: The automatic website token is managed from Widget settings and cannot be rotated like a regular token.
workspace.tokensDeleted: Deleted tokens can be included in the administrator list for audit context.
workspace.adminBody: Only tenant administrators can manage plans and billing, integration tokens, widget configuration and icons, webhooks, customer answer instructions, team invitations and roles, and customer-visible document access. Regular users can still use the main workspace features allowed by the current plan.

support.conversationsBody: The Conversations area contains customer sessions, not employee playground history. Open a conversation to review customer identity, metadata, message count, status, timestamps, and the complete ordered message transcript.
support.widgetDescription: Conversation created by the hosted website widget.
support.openDescription: The customer session can still receive messages.
support.closedDescription: The session was closed by a user, API caller, or idle timeout.
support.closingBody: Closing a conversation is final for that session and emits a conversation.closed webhook when webhooks are enabled. Start a new session if the customer returns with another request.
support.assigneeText: an active workspace team member, or unassigned.
support.notesText: internal updates with author and creation time.
support.openText: A customer or integration creates a ticket. New tickets default to an open support state.
support.triageText: Set priority and assign an owner. Add internal notes with relevant investigation context.
support.workText: Move the ticket to IN_PROGRESS while the request is actively handled.
support.closeText: Use RESOLVED when the issue has an answer, then CLOSED when no more support work is expected.
support.lifecycleNote: Ticket status does not automatically close its source conversation, and closing a conversation does not automatically resolve its tickets. Manage both lifecycles deliberately.
support.filtersBody: Search ticket title, description, and customer details, then narrow the list by status, priority, source, assigned user, unassigned state, and created date. Sort direction and pagination are preserved in the list controls.
support.notesSecurity: Ticket notes are workspace-only operational context. Do not use notes as a customer reply channel.

analyticsTeam.dashboardBody: The standard dashboard summarizes total documents, documents added this week, user messages this month compared with the previous month, stored document bytes against the storage limit, active users, and recent uploads.
analyticsTeam.dashboardNote: Dashboard totals are workspace-level operational summaries. They are available independently of the Pro advanced analytics feature.
analyticsTeam.analyticsBody: Advanced analytics adds conversations, average assistant response time, closed-session rate, user messages, daily message volume, popular questions, and—within the customer scope—resolved ticket rate.
analyticsTeam.analyticsComparison: Each headline metric includes the previous comparable period or percentage-point change. A higher response-time change means responses became slower, while a higher closed or resolved rate generally indicates more completed support work.
analyticsTeam.customerDescription: Widget and Custom API activity, including resolved ticket rate.
analyticsTeam.allDescription: Combined customer and employee chat activity.
analyticsTeam.userRole: Uses core workspace features such as documents, employee chat, dashboard, conversations, tickets, and analytics when entitled.
analyticsTeam.adminRole: Also manages users, invitations, customer-visible documents, answer instructions, widget settings, tokens, webhooks, plans, and billing.
analyticsTeam.inviteText: Choose an email and either USER or TENANT_ADMIN. Team-member quotas are enforced when inviting.
analyticsTeam.followUpText: Pending or expired invitations can be resent; pending invitations can be cancelled.
analyticsTeam.manageText: Administrators can change another member's role or set the account to INACTIVE.
analyticsTeam.reactivateText: Restoring an inactive member is subject to the current team-member quota.
analyticsTeam.deactivationSecurity: Deactivation revokes that user's refresh tokens. Use it when a teammate leaves or access should stop immediately without deleting historical ownership data.
analyticsTeam.selfRole: An administrator cannot change their own role.
analyticsTeam.selfDeactivate: An administrator cannot deactivate their own account.
analyticsTeam.finalAdmin: The final active tenant administrator cannot be demoted or deactivated.
analyticsTeam.secondAdmin: Promote a second trusted administrator before changing the only active administrator.

api.proNote: Creating or using an api:chat token requires Pro. Token management is tenant administrator-only.
api.authenticationBody: Create an integration token in Settings → Tokens with the api:chat scope. Send it on every request:
api.authenticationSecurity: Use the Custom API from trusted server code. Never place an api:chat token in a browser bundle, mobile binary, URL, log entry, or source repository.
api.localeDescription: Conversation locale; the workspace default is used when omitted.
api.sessionResponse: The response uses snake_case identifiers: id, chatbot_id, knowledge_base_id, tenant_id, and locale.
api.historyBody: History returns up to 50 messages in sequence order. Each item contains role, content, citations, optional sequence_number, and optional action.
api.closeBody: Closing is idempotent and returns 204 No Content. A closed customer conversation appears as closed in the support workspace and emits conversation.closed.
api.idempotencyUnique: Send a unique Idempotency-Key for each message creation and ticket creation operation.
api.idempotencyReuse: Reuse the same key only when retrying the same logical operation after a timeout or transport failure.
api.requestId: Send X-Request-ID on message requests to correlate application and CacaNode logs.
api.sessionReplay: Session creation does not currently accept an idempotency header; avoid automatically replaying it unless your integration reconciles the returned session ID.
api.ticketBody: A ticket must reference a session authorized by the same integration context. The external ticket DTO uses camelCase fields.
api.citationsBody: Citation fields are snake_case and can describe text, pages, sections, spreadsheet ranges, and tables. Fields that do not apply are omitted or null.
api.citationsSecurity: public_url is a signed, temporary web link. It is issued only for completed CUSTOMER_AND_EMPLOYEE documents and remains usable only while the integration token, workspace, chatbot, knowledge base, and document are eligible. Treat it as customer-accessible evidence, not a permanent document URL.

webhooks.requirementsBody: Webhook creation, testing, delivery, and secret rotation require Pro and administrator access. Saved endpoints are preserved when Pro lapses, but delivery is disabled.
webhooks.startedDescription: A Widget or Custom API customer session was created.
webhooks.closedDescription: A customer session was closed explicitly or by idle timeout.
webhooks.ticketDescription: A support ticket was created from a customer session.
webhooks.destinationSecurity: Production destinations must use HTTPS and cannot resolve to private, loopback, link-local, or site-local network addresses. Redirects are not followed.
webhooks.idDescription: id is the event identifier and is also sent as X-Cacanode-Event-Id.
webhooks.ticketData: ticket.created data contains ticketId, conversationId, chatbotId, customerEmail, title, and status. Conversation events contain conversationId, chatbotId, channel, and externalUserId; idle closures also include reason: "idle_timeout".
webhooks.signatureBody: CacaNode computes HMAC-SHA256(secret, timestamp + "." + rawBody) and sends the lowercase hexadecimal digest as X-Cacanode-Signature: v1=<hex>. The Unix-seconds timestamp is in X-Cacanode-Timestamp.
webhooks.signatureWarning: Verify against the exact raw request body bytes before JSON parsing. Re-serializing JSON can change whitespace or key order and invalidate the signature. Also reject timestamps outside your replay-tolerance window.
webhooks.deliveryBody: Your endpoint must return any 2xx status within the delivery timeout. All other responses, timeouts, DNS failures, and connection failures count as unsuccessful.
webhooks.attempts: CacaNode attempts an event up to five times.
webhooks.delays: Failed attempts are retried with increasing delays (approximately 1, 5, 25, then 125 minutes).
webhooks.allEndpoints: Each subscribed endpoint is attempted; the event completes only after all selected deliveries succeed or the attempt limit is reached.
webhooks.idempotent: Make processing idempotent by storing the event ID before applying side effects.
webhooks.testingBody: Use Send test to queue a signed test payload for one endpoint. The signing secret is shown only when an endpoint is created or its secret is rotated.
webhooks.rotationSecurity: For rotation without downtime, deploy code that can temporarily validate both the current and new secret, rotate in CacaNode, update your secret store, confirm a test delivery, and then remove the old value.
